Expectation1: Help out during difficult times or emergencies.
Situation1: You get a frantic call from your friend whose car has broken down on the side of the highway late at night, and they need you to come get them immediately.
Expectation2: Greet clients and make them feel comfortable
Situation2: A familiar customer strolls in while the receptionist is free to chat.
Story: My phone buzzed just as I was sweeping up after my last appointment. It was Jamie, my oldest friend, her voice shaky and urgent. “My car broke down on the highway. I’m scared. Can you come get me? Please?” My heart lurched—I could hear the panic in her voice, and I knew she wouldn’t call unless it was serious. I glanced at the clock; it was late, but not quite closing time. Just then, Mrs. Patel, one of my regulars, walked in, smiling and ready for her usual trim. The receptionist was at the desk, but I knew Mrs. Patel always expected me to greet her personally, to chat and make her feel at home. I could see her looking around, waiting for that warm welcome. My mind raced. Jamie needed me, but Mrs. Patel expected the comfort and attention she always got from me. I felt torn, my stomach twisting as I tried to figure out how to be the friend Jamie needed and the hairdresser Mrs. Patel counted on—all at the same time.
